newsitem.title: USA: Alaska seeks court order against Greenpeace.
newsitem.headline: Alaska seeks court order against Greenpeace.

text.p: The state of Alaska Thursday sought a restraining order against Greenpeace, which is trying to prevent Atlantic Richfield Co from moving a mobile oil drilling rig in the Arctic Ocean, a spokesman for Alaska Governor Tony Knowles said.

ARCO earlier in the day filed a similar request in U.S. District Court in Anchorage against the environmental group, which has attempted to block the company from moving the rig to a new drilling area in the Beaufort Sea.
"Alaska filed a restraining order as well. We expect these two requests, which are essentially identical, to be heard together," Bob King, Knowles spokesman said.
"It's basically to prevent them from interfering with the movement of the vessel," he said.
King said the court was expected to hold a hearing later Thursday or Friday morning.

A federal judge on Wednesday in Los Angeles, where ARCO is based, rejected Greenpeace's lawsuit to stop the company from moving the rig for exploratory drilling in the Beaufort Sea, near the Arctic National Wildlife Reserve.
Greenpeace protesters remained aboard a vessel Thursday attempting to block ARCO from moving the rig which was in waters near the Prudhoe Bay oil field.
A Greenpeace spokeswoman in Washington, Kalee Kreider, said the vessel was obeying the Coast Guard's demand to maintain a "safety zone" away from the rig.
Greenpeace maintains that moving the rig to the new site would disturb marine mammals and threaten the wildlife refuge.
"We had an hour-long conversation with the governor of Alaska. He asked us to cease and desist our activities, and we said ARCO should cease and desist their activities," Kreider said.
